# watchpoint_vault_secret (Resource)

An encrypted vault secret referenced in monitors via `{{vault.KEY}}` interpolation. The `value` is write-only: it is never read back from the API, so changing it out-of-band is not detected.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "watchpoint_vault_secret" "example" {
  key         = "STRIPE_API_KEY"
  value       = var.stripe_api_key
  description = "Production Stripe secret"
  category    = "api-keys"
}

# Or link the secret instead of storing it. Watchpoint keeps the reference and
# reads the value from your own vault when a check needs it, so the value never
# lands in Terraform state either. Rotating it on your side takes effect with no
# Terraform change at all, because the version is left unpinned.
resource "watchpoint_vault_secret" "linked_stripe_key" {
  key         = "STRIPE_API_KEY_LINKED"
  description = "Read from our own AWS Secrets Manager"

  external_vault = watchpoint_external_vault.aws.slug
  external_name  = "prod/stripe"
  external_field = "api_key"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `key` (String) Unique key within the tenant, used in `{{vault.KEY}}` interpolation.

### Optional

- `category` (String) Grouping category: `credential`, `token`, `certificate`, or `other`. Defaults to `credential`.
- `description` (String) Human-readable description of what this secret is for.
- `external_field` (String) Selects one key out of a structured secret, so `{{vault.KEY}}` injects just that value. Leave unset to use the whole secret.
- `external_name` (String) Name of the secret inside that vault, in the vendor's own addressing: a Key Vault secret name, an AWS secret name or ARN, a Vault path under the configured mount, a Conjur variable id, or `<system id>/<account id>` for BeyondTrust Password Safe.
- `external_vault` (String) The `slug` of a `watchpoint_external_vault` this secret is read from, instead of storing a value here. Watchpoint keeps only the reference and fetches the value when a check needs it, so nothing sensitive ends up in Terraform state either. Requires `external_name`; conflicts with `value`.
- `external_version` (String) Pin a specific version. Leave unset to follow whatever is current, so your own rotation takes effect with no Terraform change at all, which is usually what you want.
- `value` (String, Sensitive) Secret value. Write-only: the provider sends it on create/update but never refreshes it on read, so it is not drift-detected. Omit on update to change only metadata. Conflicts with `external_vault`; set one or the other.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Creation timestamp (RFC 3339).
- `engine` (String) `builtin` when Watchpoint holds the encrypted value, otherwise the vendor kind answering for this key.
- `has_value` (Boolean) Whether the secret currently has a stored value.
- `id` (String) Vault secret ID.
- `updated_at` (String) Last-update timestamp (RFC 3339).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import watchpoint_vault_secret.example vlt_abc123
```
